components.name: Instrument step
components.description: A square diagram step that lights up when pointed at, focused or tapped.
components.css: .ds-step { all: unset; cursor: pointer; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 18px; background: rgba(14,4,3,.72); border: 1px solid rgba(255,217,207,.18); transition: border-color .25s ease, background-color .25s ease, box-shadow .25s ease; } .ds-step:hover, .ds-step.on { border-color: #ffb05a; background: rgba(40,10,4,.82); box-shadow: 0 0 28px rgba(233,93,70,.25); } .ds-step:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffb05a; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-tag { font: 600 11px 'Archivo Variable', sans-serif; font-stretch: 62%; letter-spacing: .16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #e95d46; } .ds-name { font: 300 24px Charlton, serif; color: #fff1ec; }

components.name: Question button
components.description: Asks the ARGO console a question; pressed state shows the running question.
components.html: <button class="ds-q" aria-pressed="true">Where has this float travelled?</button>
components.css: .ds-q { all: unset; cursor: pointer; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 10px 14px; font: 14px 'Archivo Variable', sans-serif; color: #fff4e0; border: 1px solid rgba(255,230,194,.28); background: rgba(18,12,6,.7); transition: border-color .2s ease, background-color .2s ease, transform .2s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1); } .ds-q::before { content: ''; width: 7px; height: 7px; border-top: 1.5px solid #f58e12; border-right: 1.5px solid #f58e12; transform: rotate(45deg); } .ds-q:hover { border-color: #ca8334; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-q[aria-pressed='true'] { border-color: #f58e12; background: rgba(72,37,6,.75); color: #fff; } .ds-q:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f58e12; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Tab
components.description: Square condensed-caps tab for 'also in the project' rows.
components.css: .ds-tab { all: unset; cursor: pointer; padding: 7px 11px; font: 600 11px 'Archivo Variable', sans-serif; font-stretch: 62%; letter-spacing: .12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: rgba(255,230,194,.7); border: 1px solid rgba(255,230,194,.2); transition: color .2s ease, border-color .2s ease, background-color .2s ease; } .ds-tab:hover { color: #fff; border-color: #ca8334; } .ds-tab[aria-selected='true'] { color: #fff; border-color: #f58e12; background: rgba(72,37,6,.6); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f58e12; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Corner label
components.description: Poster-style caps fixed to a screen corner.
components.css: .ds-corner { margin: 0; font: 600 12px/1.25 'Archivo Variable', sans-serif; font-stretch: 62%; letter-spacing: .06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #ebe8da; }

components.name: Instrument plate
components.description: Dark square control panel that hosts a working project piece.
components.css: .ds-plate { padding: 20px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(26,17,8,.9), rgba(14,9,4,.93)); border: 1px solid rgba(255,230,194,.16); box-shadow: 0 24px 60px -20px rgba(0,0,0,.8); display: grid; gap: 6px; } .ds-plate .ds-tag { font: 600 11px 'Archivo Variable', sans-serif; font-stretch: 62%; letter-spacing: .16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f58e12; } .ds-num { font: 500 56px/0.9 'Noto Serif Display Variable', serif; font-stretch: 62.5%; color: #fff4e0; text-shadow: 0 0 .3em rgba(245,142,18,.5); }

narrative.overview:
The site is a camera shutter left open over one city night. Light is the material: streaks, glow, neon and reflections on water. The visitor scrolls through a single continuous exposure told in three colour chapters, I · Signal (red), II · Reflection (gold) and III · Clarity (cool neon), each graded to match the client's own photographs. Chapters never cut; one image always dissolves into the next through a transition born from the photograph itself (rain on the rooftop, tiles on the grid, a rising tide on the river).

The photographs are the stage and stay visible: one fullscreen WebGL canvas draws them, sharpened and alive, and every section sits on top of it with the lightest scrim that keeps type readable. Typography is poster-like and enormous at the chapter moments, then precise and small for the facts. Interface pieces are instruments in the dark: square-edged plates with fine lines that light up in the chapter's glow when touched, so the work is shown operating rather than described.
keyCharacteristics: One fullscreen photograph at a time, always visible, transitioning by its own physics.
Three palettes, one per chapter; the comet cursor and every accent follow the chapter in view.
Giant poster type for chapters and names; condensed caps for labels; a readable sans for facts.
Square instrument plates, 1px rules, glow only as a response to state.
Every project demonstrates its mechanism through interaction.

rules.name: The Chapter Rule
rules.body: Accents come only from the chapter in view. A gold accent never appears in Chapter I, a red one never in Chapter II. The comet cursor changes palette at the chapter boundary.

rules.name: The Photograph First Rule
rules.body: A scrim may darken a photograph for reading but never bury it: project screens keep the photograph at 0.8 or more brightness; full-strength behind chapter titles.

rules.name: The Two Scales Rule
rules.body: Type is either enormous (a single word or number that owns the screen) or small and precise. Nothing in between competes with the hero word of a screen.

rules.name: The Light-Not-Lift Rule
rules.body: Elements never lift on shadow ramps. State is shown by light: the border turns the chapter glow, the plate warms, a soft glow appears.

dos: Do keep every fact traceable to the CV; label illustrations as illustrations on screen.
Do give each project an interaction that shows its mechanism working.
Do transition between chapter photographs with an effect drawn from the photograph (rain, grid tiles, tide), through the shared backdrop controller.
Do use the chapter's palette for every accent and switch the comet palette at the chapter boundary.
Do keep pieces square with 1px hairlines and show state with light.
Do ship reduced-motion final states for every animation.
donts: Don't use the hero-metric template (big number, small label, supporting stats) on its own as a project screen.
Don't use meaningless section numbers or a/b/c bullet cards as structure.
Don't bury the photograph under a heavy scrim.
Don't use rounded cards, glassmorphism, gradient text or emoji icons.
Don't publish the phone number, or invent results, links or testimonials.
Don't use Inter, Geist, Space Grotesk or Instrument Serif.
